description_full: Sunny Optical Technology (Group) Company Limited, an investment holding company, engages in designing, researching, developing, manufacturing, and selling optical and optical related products, and scientific instruments. It operates through Optical Components, Optoelectronic Products, and Optical Instruments segments. The Optical Components segment offers vehicle lens sets and optical parts for vehicle light detection and ranging, handset lens sets, glass spherical and aspherical lenses for digital cameras, and other optical components. The Optoelectronic Products segment provides XR visual modules, smart glass camera modules, robotic vision subsystems, handset camera modules, and other optoelectronic products. The Optical Instruments segment offers intelligent equipment and microscopes. It also offers mobile phone products and solutions; automotive lens, headlight, HUD, LiDAR, optical elements, automotive camera modules, and active safety warning systems; infrared thermal imaging lens, surveillance lens, and video conference lens; and mobile phone parts inspection and automotive camera module manufacturing equipment. In addition, the company provides life science, industrial inspection, metallurgical, polarization, and stereo microscope instruments; image analysis software; AR/VR optic components and sensors, and system modules; location and recognition systems; and microbes and pathological medical inspection devices. The company operates in China, rest of Asia, Europe, North America, and internationally. Sunny Optical Technology (Group) Company Limited was founded in 1984 and is headquartered in Yuyao, China.

financial_summary: Sunny Optical Technology (Group is a mid-cap technology business with a $8.9B market cap on $6.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +7% over the past three years, a respectable pace for a business of this size.

Returns on capital run at 27% against a 10% cost of capital — a 17-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, and 19% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $472M in free cash flow — roughly 7 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.31× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 8.6×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.8%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
